trials.selection_rationale: Decode dominates the objective: the clean original baseline (inputs/project.json) is end_to_end_ms 694.01 with ttft_ms 24.29 (constraint <= 25.50) and decode_ms 669.79, so the 31 cached decode steps are 96.5% of end_to_end_ms. Two independent diagnostics on this exact revision (3701b7f2...) show decode is host-dispatch-bound, not GPU-bound: execution_timeline (observations/current/execution_timeline-1221e205.json, workload window incl. final sync) measures only 365.4 ms of GPU-busy time inside the decode window, with 64,294 decode kernels (~2,074 per decode step, avg 5.7 us each), i.e. the GPU sits idle while Python submits the next step; python_runtime (observations/current/python_runtime-aea48e29.json) shows 17,472 nn.Module _wrapped_call_impl calls per invocation (~546 per forward), modeling_qwen3.py RMSNorm.forward 310.6 ms cumulative, linear host dispatch 100.5 ms over 8,096 calls and Tensor.to 78.9 ms over 9,376 calls. Clean-run arithmetic gives ~365-375 ms of decode GPU work vs 669.8 ms decode wall: ~300 ms (~45% of end_to_end) is host-side dispatch gap, about twice the size of any achievable kernel-time saving, while prefill is already nearly GPU-bound (21.4 ms GPU busy vs 24.3 ms clean TTFT) and TTFT has only 5% headroom. I therefore select the single coherent editable boundary that owns the entire decode computation: the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM whole-forward module group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f (call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations, signature input_ids [1,1] + DynamicCache + use_cache=True + logits_to_keep=1). Replacing this whole bundle explicitly covers every inherited call inside it (Qwen3Model decode, 36 decoder layers, attention/MLP/RMSNorm, all 253 decode aten::linear sites, sdpa, cat, rotary), so per the binding contract the inherited per-call requirements are waived at this boundary, and per the contract's phase/signature guards the same model instance's prefill call (900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a, input_ids [1,256], no past_key_values) stays on the original path, protecting TTFT. Smaller scopes were rejected on measured evidence: functional groups (aten::linear/sdpa/cat) are 5.7 us-average kernels where legacy-backend functional dispatch would add cost rather than remove it; layer-level groups would still leave ~546 module calls per step of Python overhead in the timed loop.

trials.selection_rationale: Measured facts: the clean original baseline (inputs/project.json) is end_to_end_ms 694.01 with ttft_ms 24.285 (constraint limit 1.05x = 25.499) and decode_ms 669.79, so the 31 cached decode steps are 96.5% of the objective; decode is host-dispatch-bound (execution_timeline: 386.8 ms kernel active union vs 1080 ms gaps in the profiled window; python_runtime: transformers module dispatch ~911 ms cumulative in an 836 ms window). The previous bundle trial-7cbb441641 (parent 3701b7f2, group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f, call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, static-cache CUDA-graph decode engine) was quality-clean (max_abs_error 0.0, 62/62 graph_replay, 0 fallbacks, exact greedy tokens) and improved the objective to 378.90 ms vs reference 701.62 (paired gains 343.1/302.3 ms, both above the 6.6/4.4 ms noise bounds), but was rejected only for 'original_baseline_constraint_failed': ttft medians [25.857, 24.950] vs limit 25.499 - one endpoint 0.36 ms over. That failure is a margin problem, not a proven systematic prefill slowdown: binding_cost diagnostics on the same revision show parent-arm ttft medians [26.51, 24.19] and passthrough-arm [24.19, 25.64] with samples spanning 24.12-30.13 ms, so worker ttft noise (~1.5 ms) exceeds the 1.21 ms headroom an unchanged prefill has below the limit; the same candidate measured ttft 24.67 in its screening trial. Re-running the identical design gambles on noise. The repair must create real ttft margin: prefill CUDA kernel time is 21.563 ms (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f) against 24.285 ms clean ttft wall, i.e. ~2.7 ms of per-kernel launch/dispatch cost (253 aten::linear, 36 layers, norms, rotary) plus per-invocation DynamicCache allocation inside the timed window - exactly the cost class the decode graphs already removed (decode 669.8 -> 353.4 ms with the same kernel floor). Therefore extend the same engine to the prefill boundary: one static KV cache written by a captured prefill graph (positions 0..255) and consumed by the 31 per-position decode graphs (256..286). The two edits need one another (shared static cache, shared graph pool, decode cache-identity short-circuit that eliminates the 72-copy import), so they are one joint candidate at the coherent editable boundary Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward for both phases; both source completion boundaries, workload, precision and quality checks stay in the frozen adapter and are untouched.

trials.selection_rationale: Measured facts: the current accepted version (revision f03e6f70, bundle trial-f71b5c1677-param-401aa647 installed at the two Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward boundaries) measures end_to_end_ms 374.19 with ttft_ms 21.357/21.411 against the 25.499 limit (project.json, previous-feedback project_measurement; noise bounds 2.9/11.8 ms). Host dispatch is no longer the bottleneck: execution_timeline shows kernel_active_union 378.07 of 385.45 ms span with only 7.38 ms gaps; python_runtime shows 32 graph replays costing 0.95 ms total self time with the host blocked in cuda_synchronize; device_telemetry samples 100% GPU and 90% memory utilization during the workload window. The decode module group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f (call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations) contributes 356.6 ms diagnostic CUDA (95% of the objective) and the prefill group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f (call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a) 21.0 ms. call-resources.json decomposes the 31 decode steps (63953 kernels, ~2073/step): cuBLAS gemv variants take 279.7 ms (9.02 ms/step) streaming ~8.05 GB of BF16 weights per step, i.e. ~892 GB/s or ~88% of the RTX 4090's 1008 GB/s peak - the GEMVs are near the bandwidth limit and are not the opportunity. The remaining 76.9 ms (2.48 ms/step, 21.6% of decode CUDA time) is non-GEMV kernel overhead: per step 145 RMSNorm chains each expanded into mean-reduce + pow + rsqrt + mul + mul + bf16-cast (~6 kernels), RoPE rotate_half as 72 cat + 72 neg + 216 mul + adds, 144 residual adds, ~217 copies/casts, silu+mul, plus pytorch_flash split-kv fwd+combine pairs (1116+1116 kernels, 9.16 ms total, ~6x their 42.5 MB/step KV-read floor for a single-query GQA step). These ~2100 one-to-three-microsecond kernels per step are pure fusion headroom that does not require exceeding the already-saturated weight-streaming bandwidth. Opportunity: rewrite the decode step inside the engine's CUDA graphs with fused kernels - fused RMSNorm(+cast), fused RoPE rotate+K/V cache write, fused residual-add+norm, fused SiLU-mul, and a single-pass GQA decode-attention kernel replacing split-kv+combine - while keeping the proven engine skeleton (per-position graphs, static [36,1,8,288,128] cache, publish/import, parent fallback, bitwise installation validation that previously held max_abs_error 0.0), the near-peak cuBLAS GEMVs, and the accepted prefill graph replay verbatim. Boundary choice: the two edits need one another (shared static KV cache, shared graph pool, cache-identity short-circuit across the prefill-to-decode handoff), and replacing the whole accepted bundle at both module sites avoids coupling to the inherited engine's published cache vessel (which would reintroduce the per-invocation 42 MB import copy the accepted bundle eliminated), so this is one joint candidate at the same coherent editable boundary as the accepted bundle; the adapter loop's argmax/cat/clone/copy_ calls outside these boundaries are untouched. Fallback safety: any fusion that fails bitwise installation validation or the signature/cache/position guards falls back to the parent forward, leaving quality unchanged and only losing speed.
